526: ## A4.8 TDD for Logic-Bearing Code ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
527: 
528: **Test integrity (binding, §V2 VERIFICATION_UPGRADES):** tests are READ-ONLY
529: during implementation — never weaken/delete/skip a failing test to make it
530: pass; a test↔spec conflict is FLAGGED (PAUSED/ADR), never cheated green.
531: 
532: **Core principle: if you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it
533: tests the right thing.** A test written after the code passes immediately —
534: it may test the wrong thing, the implementation instead of the behavior, or
535: miss the edge case you didn't think of.
536: 
537: **Scope:** logic-bearing code (services/repositories/utils, transforms,
538: validation, state) — test-first · UI/E2E rendering — §A4.1 screenshot loop ·
539: backend API — §A4.7 (NEW endpoints test-first) · pure config/markup/docs,
540: generated code — exempt (state the reason).
541: 
542: **Trusted oracle (what may certify a task, in order):** ① project/external
543: acceptance tests — the only certifying tier (greenfield: render the acceptance
544: criteria executable; else the log records `- oracle: self-tests (weak)` and
545: the claim is flagged); ② independently generated + **qualified** tests (fail
546: on the stub, pass on a known-correct solution, fail on a plausible wrong
547: solution) — weak tier: catches gross errors, never certifies; ③ self-written
548: tests — weakest. Record the tier in `verification_log.md`:
549: `- oracle: project-tests | executable-acceptance | qualified-generated | self-tests (weak)`.
550: **Under-specified contract:** a required behavior whose interface/semantics are
551: not visible in the spec/starter is NOT invented — record it as an open question
552: and resolve it (GUIDED) or mark the criterion unverified (AUTO ADR); a test
553: that invents an interface is a false oracle. **Checker contract:** a project
554: checker (`script/check.sh` / `tests/check.py`) is the loop's feedback — quote
555: its pass line, never edit tests to pass. Templates: APPENDIX §A4.8.
556: 
557: **The cycle (RED → GREEN → minimal):**
558: 1. **RED — write ONE failing test** for the next small behavior. One
559:    behavior per test, clear name, real code (mocks only when unavoidable).
560: 2. **Verify RED — run it and WATCH it fail:** it fails (not errors), for the
561:    expected reason (missing feature, not a typo). A test passing immediately
562:    tests existing behavior — fix it. **Paste the failing output into
563:    `tests/verification_log.md`** (the RED evidence for COV-1 / Gate 1).
564: 3. **GREEN — minimal code to pass** (YAGNI, nothing beyond the test).
565: 4. **Verify GREEN — it passes**, and the rest of the suite stays green.
566: 5. **Commit**, then next failing test.
567: 
568: **Wrote code before the test?** Delete it, start from the test — keeping it as
569: "reference" is test-after in disguise.
570: 
571: **Regression tests — the red-green verification method:** a regression test is
572: only proven if it can catch the bug:
573: ```
574: Write test → run (PASSES with fix present) → revert the fix → run (MUST FAIL)
575: → restore the fix → run (passes)
576: ```
577: A regression test never watched failing on the buggy code is unproven.
578: 
579: **Red flags — STOP:** code before test · test passes on first run with no
580: nameable production change that would break it · "too simple to test" /
581: "test after" / "already verified manually" · **the verification reference
582: shares the candidate's assumptions** (§A4.10 TRUST-AND-VERIFY).

586: ## A4.9 Independent Code Review (Major Changes)
587: 
588: This is the canonical text of COV-8. The maker/checker split covers
589: screenshots — but the CODE itself is otherwise only ever seen by the model
590: that wrote it. For major changes, dispatch an independent reviewer BEFORE
591: the A4.4 completion table (and AFTER Gate-1 test evidence exists). For minor
592: changes: state `A4.9 not triggered — reason: <…>` in the [Verification Gate]
593: line and proceed. **Lane L default: TWO adversarial fresh-context reviewers
594: (§V4 VERIFICATION_UPGRADES)** — merged findings, solo findings still
595: adjudicated, reviewer disagreement escalates.
596: 
597: **Trigger ANY of:** new feature · ≥3 files changed · schema/API-surface change ·
598: security-sensitive area · **behavior-semantic change** (a one-line diff can
599: still be a behavior change).
600: **"Files changed" counts EVERY path in `git diff --stat $BASE..$HEAD`** —
601: tests, docs, and config included; "only core logic files changed" is NOT a
602: valid reduction. **Skip for:** mechanical
603: single-file bugfixes with NO behavior-semantic change, copy/style tweaks,
604: config edits — each `A4.9 not triggered` reason in the gate line must cite
605: `git diff --stat` output, not self-recollection. **Risk-tier paths —
606: non-skippable:** when the diff touches a code path matching
607: `(?i)(^|/)(auth|security|payments?|billing|crypto|migrations?|permissions?|acl)(/|\.|_|$)`
608: (code extensions only), the trigger fires REGARDLESS of file count; assert
609: group 16 machine-checks `tests/review_package.md` exists on disk.
610: 
611: **How:**
612: 1. Get the review range: `BASE_SHA` = baseline commit (C2 Step 5), `HEAD_SHA` =
613:    final commit. Write `git log --oneline $BASE..$HEAD`, `git diff --stat`, and
614:    `git diff -U10 $BASE..$HEAD` to ONE file (e.g. `tests/review_package.md`) —
615:    hand the reviewer the FILE, keeping the diff out of your own context.
616: 2. Dispatch a reviewer subagent (opencode `task` tool) with: the file path,
617:    the acceptance criteria / requirements (or `tests/acceptance.md` path), the
618:    CODING_PRINCIPLES.md §Reviewer Smell Baseline, and
619:    this verdict contract — **Strengths · Issues (Critical / Important / Minor,
620:    each tagged with its dimension — `Bugs` (logic/edge cases) · `Security`
621:    (injection/authz/secrets/attacker-controlled input) · `Compliance`
622:    (spec-fidelity: requirements missing/partial · scope creep ·
623:    looks-implemented-but-wrong, quoting the criterion/spec line) — with
624:    file:line + why it matters) · Assessment (ready / ready-with-fixes / not ready)**.
625:    **Minor findings are itemized at
626:    most 5, the rest summarized as a count** (nit cap); generated paths and
627:    anything already mechanically enforced (hooks, assert groups) are out of
628:    scope. The reviewer is READ-ONLY.
629: 3. Act on the verdict (fix-round loop):
630:    - **Critical** → fix now; re-run covering tests; scoped re-review (Step 4).
631:    - **Important** → fix before the completion table; re-run covering tests;
632:      scoped re-review.
633:    - **Minor** → record in memory as deferred; point it out in the completion
634:      table. Minor never enters the fix loop.
635:    - **Fix-round loop:** one round = one fix dispatch + one scoped re-review
636:      (Step 4). Max **5 rounds** per review wave. Reuse A4.1's stall rule
637:      (same finding ≥3 consecutive rounds → apply §A4.10). At the cap,
638:      **adjudicate each open finding yourself** — you hold the cross-task
639:      context the reviewer lacks: park with a ruling (`parked — <finding> —
640:      ruling: <why the code stands>`), or if load-bearing (a later task builds
641:      on it / it reveals a plan defect) STOP and escalate. Critical/Important
642:      findings MUST be fixed or parked-with-ruling before the A4.4 completion
643:      table. A silent discard is forbidden — every ruling is a recorded entry.
644: 4. **Scoped re-review:** regenerate the review package over the fix range —
645:    `git diff $FIX_BASE..$HEAD` where `$FIX_BASE` = the head the previous
646:    review saw — and re-dispatch the reviewer with the new package plus the
647:    open-findings list. The re-review verdicts each finding
648:    **ADDRESSED / NOT ADDRESSED** and flags NEW breakage in the fix diff only;
649:    out-of-scope observations become deferred Minors and never extend the loop.
650: 5. **Disagreement is allowed** — a technically wrong finding gets a reasoned
651:    push-back (cite working tests/code), recorded as a ruling; never silently
652:    discard.
653: 6. **Findings feed the rules:** a mistake flagged twice goes into project
654:    memory (feedback/⛔ per A7.9) or `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, so it is caught at
655:    generation time, not review.
656: 
657: **Red flags:** skipping review because "it's simple" · fixing findings without
658: re-running tests · accepting every suggestion without verifying it against the
659: codebase.

663: ## A4.10 Stall Escape: Parameterize · Differential-Test · Dual-Path
664: 
665: Companion to COV-7 (`cap=5 stall=3×`). COV-7 decides WHEN a loop must stop;
666: this section decides WHAT TO DO at that stop. A stall followed by "retry,
667: slightly different" is the same spin with new vowels. Mechanisms adapted
668: from J-Space Cognition Suite (see repo README → Attribution).
669: 
670: ### DROWNING DETECTION — recognize it early
671: 
672: Stall signals: the same sub-problem re-derived with no new constraint ·
673: constraints flip-flopping between iterations · the same test failing with a
674: mobile but related error · three failed fixes on the same problem (§A4.6
675: escalation) · **≥4 consecutive no-op bash calls** — bare `echo`/`printf`
676: narration markers standing in for an announced tool call; the loop-guard's
677: `noop-bash` finding interrupts this mechanically, and the interrupt itself
678: IS a stall declaration (log `- stall: noop-bash …` and take the escape
679: below). **≥4 consecutive identical tool calls** (same tool + canonical args,
680: MCP included; pid re-observations don't count) → `identical-tool-run`
681: interrupt. `tool-frequency` needs explicit `loopGuardToolFrequencyMin`;
682: bulk work isn't a loop. Interrupts are stall declarations
683: (log `- stall: <kind> …`, take the escape below). **Any two signals → declare
684: the stall explicitly in the log**
685: (`- stall: <signals> — stopping pure iteration`). An undeclared stall
686: becomes silent guessing, which looks exactly like reasoning right up until
687: it is wrong.
688: 
689: ### PARAMETRIZE — make the unknown finite (before the next direction is chosen)
690: 
691: 1. Name exactly what the failed iterations could not settle. One unknown per
692:    line, in the log.
693: 2. Enumerate plausible values as a **finite candidate set** (`timeout ∈
694:    {30s, 60s, 120s}`; `the bug is in {routing, auth middleware, handler,
695:    serializer}`). If the set will not go finite, discretize the dimension
696:    that matters and say what was dropped — an unbounded unknown cannot be
697:    tested.
698: 3. Every candidate stays live until evidence kills it. A killed candidate
699:    gets recorded with the evidence that killed it (→ memory ❌ per
700:    MEMORY_RULES.md §A7.7). No premature favourites.
701: 4. Name **the cheapest test that could refute each candidate** (a test that
702:    cannot fail is a ceremony).
703: 
704: ### TRUST-AND-VERIFY — differential testing with an independent reference
705: 
706: When the verification itself is in doubt (the candidate "works" but you
707: cannot trust the check):
708: 
709: 1. **Build the reference** — the simplest independent procedure whose
710:    assumptions are explicit and separately checked: brute force, exhaustive
711:    enumeration, a second data path, a hand-worked example.
712: 2. **The reference must NOT share the candidate's cleverness.** If it
713:    inherits the same assumption, it inherits the same bug and will agree
714:    with the candidate beautifully while both are wrong. Where they must
715:    share an assumption, test that assumption separately and say so.
716: 3. **Differential-test:** same inputs to both. Compare outputs. Sweep small,
717:    edge (empty, single, maximum, degenerate) and randomized cases where
718:    cheap.
719: 4. **Every mismatch is a gift** — it localizes the false assumption better
720:    than any amount of re-reading. Study the mismatch, refine, re-test.
721: 5. **State the coverage with the conclusion** — "verified" without a stated
722:    scope is not a result (machine-checked: `assert_artifacts.py` group 13).
723: 
724: ### DUAL-PATH RECONCILE — two cheap routes, compare, then commit
725: 
726: When two independent, cheap verification routes are available (read state
727: **through the API** AND **from the database**; build in `.venv` AND system
728: python; `git diff` AND `git diff --stat`), take BOTH before declaring a
729: conclusion:
730: 
731: - Where they agree → confidence is earned; record both routes in the log.
732: - Where they disagree → you have located the faulty assumption — the
733:   disagreement IS the finding. Record it and resolve from the discrepancy,
734:   not from re-reading.
735: 
736: This is the diagnosis clause's (A4.1 Step 4) source: a retry without a
737: diagnosis is the same attempt again; a diagnosis earns its cost only when it
738: is falsifiable by a second path.
739: 
740: ### SHIFT — the licensed exit moves
741: 
742: After parametrizing, the next direction MUST be one of:
743: 1. **Shift the abstraction** — the frame is fighting the facts; tighten,
744:    split, or replace it.
745: 2. **Shift the strategy** — same goal, genuinely different route (different
746:    layer, different tool, different representation).
747: 3. **Shift to empirics** — stop deriving, start measuring (this section).
748: 
749: Shifting to vagueness, to summarizing the problem, or to "let me try it
750: again" is not a licensed shift. And: if the same wall returns a **third
751: time**, the problem is mis-framed, not mis-solved — restate it in different
752: primitives (→ §A4.6 escalation to the user).

25: ## §M Operating Modes (AUTO / GUIDED)
26: 
27: Every task declares exactly one line in ZERO (§2), before any code action:
28: 
29: ```
30: Mode: AUTO        (default — agent takes over end-to-end)
31: Mode: GUIDED      (user asked for more involvement / approval points)
32: ```
33: 
34: **The modes differ ONLY in who decides Class-I questions.** Everything that
35: constitutes *evidence* is mode-invariant: COV-1 tests-executed, COV-2
36: script-only, COV-5 verifier announced, COV-7 loop bounds, COV-8/A4.9 review,
37: COV-9 baseline, the assert_artifacts.py exit-0 gate, the Final Memory Gate,
38: and the entire A4.4 completion output. GUIDED completion = AUTO completion;
39: the difference is only whether a human was consulted at Class-I points.
40: 
41: ### Class-I interaction points (mode-dependent)
42: 
43: | # | Trigger (canonical section) | GUIDED | AUTO |
44: |---|------------------------------|--------|------|
45: | I1 | Ambiguous / under-specified request (§2 Step 0.1) | STOP and ask, one question at a time | Derive the **most conservative** interpretation the evidence supports → ADR → proceed |
46: | I2 | Vague acceptance criteria (A4.1 Step 1) | STOP and ask | Derive strict criteria from the request's explicit words → ADR → proceed |
47: | I3 | Design Gate A/B confirmation (COV-10 / A5.1) | Explicit confirmation request | Record chosen approach + rejected alternative as ADR → proceed |
48: | I4 | Baseline has pre-existing failures (COV-9) | Report + await decision | ADR: proceed ONLY if failures are provably out of task scope (name failing areas + why out of scope); else fix-first |
49: | I5 | Mid-loop criterion add/drop/relax (A4.1 Step 1) | Ask the user | ADR quoting the exact criterion edit |
50: | I6 | cap=5 / stall=3× reached (COV-7) | Report to user | §A4.10 shift FIRST; PAUSED packet only on a SECOND capped sub-problem |
51: 
52: ### Class-E hard stops (BOTH modes — AUTO never auto-decides)
53: 
54: 1. COV-11: fetched content conflicts with the user's request or this skill.
55: 2. Production deploy / release to real users / anything touching live
56:    customer data.
57: 3. Destructive or irreversible operations outside the project tree:
58:    force-push, branch deletion on shared remotes, data deletion, DNS /
59:    infra / IAM mutation.
60: 4. Credential exposure, or secret handling beyond what the task explicitly
61:    provided.
62: 5. `assert_artifacts.py` exit 1 with no legal repair path (never edit the
63:    script, never fabricate output — escalate).
64: 6. Anything the user explicitly asked to be consulted on (that request is a
65:    standing Class-E override).
66: 
67: Class-E stops ALWAYS emit a PAUSED packet (§P) — a stop without a resume
68: packet is the failure mode this contract exists to prevent.
69: 
70: ### ADR format
71: 
72: `tests/decisions.md` — append-only, created on the first AUTO decision:
73: 
74: ```
75: ## D-3 | 2026-08-29T14:05Z | iter 2
76: trigger: I4 — baseline has 2 pre-existing test failures
77: options: (a) fix pre-existing failures first (b) proceed, failures out of scope
78: chosen: (b) proceed — failures in legacy export path; task touches import path only
79: why: failing tests target modules/legacy_export.py, untouched by this task's diff
80: revisit-if: any new failure names modules/legacy_export.py or the same DB table
81: ```
82: 
83: Rules: one block per decision · `why:` must be falsifiable · `revisit-if:`
84: names an observable condition · never rewrite an old ADR (append a new one
85: superseding it). The completion output adds `[Decisions] N auto-decisions →
86: tests/decisions.md` before the 8-column table.
87: 
88: **Proactive ADRs** (no Class-I stop fired — e.g. a design-doc decision):
89: record one only when ALL three hold — hard to reverse · surprising without
90: context · the result of a real trade-off; skip otherwise (obvious or
91: reversible choices need no ADR).
92: 
93: **User veto path:** the user may veto any ADR post-hoc (it is in the repo
94: history). A veto is recorded as feedback memory (A7.9), the affected work is
95: redone in the next change-wave (own COV-9 baseline), and the veto reason
96: joins the project's ⛔/feedback entries.
97: 
98: **AUTO runaway bound:** AUTO buys autonomy, not license to spin. At most ONE
99: extra autonomous direction per stop type (I6: one §A4.10 shift before any
100: pause). ≥3 ADRs on the SAME sub-problem → the next stop is a PAUSED packet
101: regardless of mode.

105: ## §P PAUSED / Resume Contract
106: 
107: Every turn that stops for a gate — either mode, Class-I or Class-E — MUST
108: end with BOTH:
109: 
110: 1. `tests/paused_state.md` written with the packet below.
111: 2. The same one-liner as the LAST line of the reply (human-visible):
112: 
113: ```
114: [PAUSED] gate=<name> | question=<one line> | options=<2-3> | default-if-continue=<option> | state=<wave, files touched, next step>
115: ```
116: 
117: Field semantics: `gate:` names the rule that fired (I4 / COV-9 · I6 /
118: cap-stall · Class-E: COV-11 …) · `options:` are the 2-3 candidate actions ·
119: `default-if-continue:` is what the agent will do on an unqualified
120: "continue" · `state:` names the change-wave, the files already touched, and
121: the literal next step.
122: 
123: **Resume semantics:** a user "continue" (or any reply that does not pick an
124: option) = approval of `default-if-continue`. It is NOT a re-plan: the agent
125: does not re-derive context, re-ask settled questions, or restart the loop.
126: On resume: delete/clear `tests/paused_state.md`, append
127: `- resumed: <default> approved` to `tests/verification_log.md`, continue from
128: `state:`. A reply that picks a DIFFERENT option overrides the default; log
129: `- resumed: <chosen option> (user override)` instead.
130: 
131: **Re-entry order after a gap** (SKILL.md §3.3): paused_state.md (if present)
132: → tests/working_note.md (if present, §A7.15 — the live hypothesis ledger)
133: → tests/acceptance.md in full → verification_log.md tail (~40 lines; full
134: read only if <200 lines or inconsistent) → §1 covenant recall. Name the pass
135: (C1/C2/C4-C8) + first action in one line before acting.
136: 
137: **Batching:** ONE packet per pause, never a drip of questions. In GUIDED,
138: all pending Class-I questions of the current phase collapse into the single
139: packet's `options:`.
140: 
141: **Frontier rounds (GUIDED, ≥2 pending Class-I questions):** the single
142: packet is one *frontier round*:
143: 1. Number each question; each carries its own recommended answer (its
144:    `default-if-continue`).
145: 2. Order by dependency — a question whose answer depends on a still-open
146:    question belongs to the NEXT round, not this one.
147: 3. **Facts vs decisions:** never ask the user for a fact discoverable from
148:    the environment (files, git, config, tools) — look it up or dispatch a
149:    subagent. A running lookup is an unsettled prerequisite: questions
150:    downstream of it wait; ask the rest of the frontier now. Only *decisions*
151:    go to the user.
152: 4. Termination: frontier empty = nothing left silently assumed → proceed.
153: 
154: This refines the per-phase collapse above; single-ambiguity clarification
155: (I1 · REFERENCE.md §A5.1 Gate A) stays one-question-at-a-time. AUTO is
156: unchanged (ADRs, no frontier).

182: ## C4. Audit (Read-Only Task)
183: 
184: **Trigger:** the primary deliverable is a review/report of an existing
185: codebase — code audit, security review, architecture assessment, migration
186: readiness check. NOT for fixing: fixes discovered by an audit become a
187: follow-up C2 task (record them in the report's remediation section).
188: 
189: **Read-only boundary:** no source, config, or script edits anywhere in the
190: target repo. Writes are limited to: `docs/AUDIT_<date>_<slug>.md`,
191: `tests/acceptance.md`, `tests/verification_log.md`, `tests/decisions.md`,
192: `memory/`. Violating the boundary voids the audit (the deliverable is
193: trust).
194: 
195: Binding order:
196: 
197: 1. `0 §2 ZERO + Mode line → 1 scope & criteria`: decompose the audit
198:    request into explicit, individually-checkable criteria — coverage areas
199:    (which modules/paths/qualities), depth, output language — into
200:    `tests/acceptance.md` (first line `> cap=5  stall=3×` preserved; COV-7
201:    bound applies to the audit pass itself). Ambiguity → Class-I rules.
202: 2. `2 READ-ONLY pass`: systematic inspection per criterion. Use search
203:    tools + reads; keep evidence quotes (file:line + 1-2 line excerpt) as you
204:    go — an audit note without a locator is not a finding candidate.

206:    dimension (`Bugs` logic/edge cases · `Security` injection/authz/secrets/
207:    attacker-controlled input · `Compliance` matches stated requirements) ·
208:    file:line · why it matters · **PoC command or quoted-code argument**.
209:    A finding without repro/quote evidence is NOT a finding — it is a
210:    hypothesis; verify or drop it. Nit cap: itemize at most 5 Minors, count
211:    the rest.

214:    list + PoCs — verdict per finding: CONFIRMED / REFUTED / UNCERTAIN.

216:    downgrade to "suspected" in the report.
217: 5. `5 report`: `docs/AUDIT_<date>_<slug>.md` — scope & method · findings
218:    (verified, with evidence) · remediation plan (ordered, each item = a

229:

240:    - baseline GREEN on the release commit (COV-9, own change-wave);

250:    To staging/dev with no real users: AUTO may proceed with an ADR (env is
251:    disposable); to production: always the PAUSED packet.
252: 4. `4 post-deploy smoke`: A4.7b real-HTTP workflow traces (1-3 business
253:    flows) against the DEPLOYED environment — `tests/workflows/*.trace.log`
254:    with the deployed URL named. `E2E depth: real-HTTP` in the gate line.
255:    Smoke failure → treat as incident (C6 triage rules), never "it worked
256:    locally".
257: 5. `5 rollback drill`: execute the rollback script ONCE against staging
258:    (or a canary), verify service returns to the previous version, re-deploy
259:    the new version. A rollback path that was never executed is a hypothesis.
260: 6. `6 completion`: A4.4 table (evidence = smoke traces + drill log) +
261:    deployment record in memory/ (date, env, version, rollback point, smoke
262:    results).

266: ## C6. Ops / Incident Workflow
267: 
268: **Trigger:** live breakage, alarms, user-reported production failure, or
269: routine maintenance waves (dependency upgrades, cert rotation, backup
270: restore checks).
271: 
272: **Incident path** (something is broken NOW):
273: 
274: 1. `0 triage FIRST — evidence before fixes (A4.6 Phase 1)`: capture the
275:    failure state (logs, metrics, error output) BEFORE touching anything;
276:    reproduce or bound the blast radius; identify the last-known-good version
277:    (git tag/commit + deploy record).
278: 2. `1 incident record`: open `docs/POSTMORTEM_<date>_<slug>.md`
279:    (APPENDIX C6 postmortem template) with trigger → timeline → impact. It is a chain
280:    artifact: cite the alert/log that started it.
281: 3. `2 hotfix via C2`: full C2 discipline with ONE relaxation — the COV-9
282:    baseline is the pre-incident commit (or last-known-good deploy), and the
283:    baseline run may be skipped if the system is DOWN (state
284:    `COV-9 skipped — active incident, system unavailable; baseline =
285:    <last-known-good>` in the log). Every other gate applies.
286: 4. `3 verify`: fix + suite green + the ORIGINAL failure evidence re-captured
287:    (the exact symptom that started the incident must be shown resolved).
288: 5. `4 postmortem`: complete the record — root cause, fix commit hash,
289:    **one permanent regression case** added to the test suite so the incident
290:    can never recur silently.
291: 6. `5 memory`: ⛔ (if ≥3 failures preceded the fix) / ❌ failed attempts /
292:    feedback per A7.9 + A4.4 completion table.
293: 
294: **Maintenance path** (nothing is broken): dependency upgrades and similar
295: waves run as C2 with a bound — **≤5 upgrades per change-wave**, each wave
296: gets its own COV-9 baseline + suite run; a red wave stops the batch (don't
297: mix 10 upgrades into one undiagnosable wave). One upgrade per commit inside
298: the wave, so bisect works.

302: ## C7. Non-Web Runtime (CLI / Library / Batch / Pipeline)
303: 
304: **Trigger:** the change's runtime surface is NOT a browser page (→ §A4.1)
305: and NOT an HTTP API (→ §A4.7): CLI output, library behavior, data pipeline,
306: batch job, daemon without HTTP.
307: 
308: **1. Profile:** write `tests/project_profile.json` in the FIRST change-wave:
309: `{"profile": "cli"}` (CLI/batch/pipeline) or `{"profile": "library"}`
310: (library). This declaratively skips structurally-N/A assert groups (see
311: Profile Reference) — every applicable group stays enforced. COV-2 applies
312: to whatever lifecycle scripts the project actually has (a library's
313: `script/` may hold only test/release helpers — that's fine; the profile
314: documents why start/stop/restart don't exist).
315: 
316: **2. Acceptance criteria over OBSERVABLE output:** each criterion names a
317: checkable runtime observation — exit code for given input · stdout/stderr
318: content (exact or pattern) · files written (path + content shape) · timing
319: bound · golden-output equality. "Works correctly" is not a criterion.
320: 
321: **3. Evidence (replaces Playwright):** per flow, save to `tests/`:
322: - invocation transcript: command line + full stdout/stderr + exit code
323:   (`tests/<flow>.run.log`);
324: - output diff against a golden file where output is deterministic
325:   (`tests/<flow>.diff`);
326: - for pipelines: the artifact produced (file path + checksum) logged.
327: Screenshots/mm-sensor do not apply: announce `Verifier: direct read
328: (non-web)` at Step 0 and cross-check every criterion against the transcript
329: + artifact on disk. assert_artifacts group 3's screenshot checks still
330: apply to any png you DO cite; group 11 checks cited media — cite none.
331: 
332: **4. §A4.8 test-first** for all logic-bearing code (a library's public API
333: IS logic-bearing): RED → GREEN per the standard cycle.
334: 
335: **5. Loop:** Act → Verify (transcript + artifacts vs criteria) → Fix → Log
336: (`verification_log.md`, `diagnosis:` on every FAIL), cap=5 / stall=3×,
337: §A4.10 on stall. For libraries also run the DOWNSTREAM check: import/use
338: the library from a throwaway consumer script (`tests/consumer_smoke.py`) —
339: green unit tests do not prove the package installs or imports.
340: 
341: **6. Completion:** A4.4 table; gate line `Verifier: direct read (non-web)` ·
342: `Loop executed: yes` · `E2E depth: service-direct` (or `unit-only` with the
343: A4.7b ladder reason).

347: ## C8. Outer-Loop Workflow (Backlog / Long-Running Batch)
348: 
349: **Trigger:** the user hands over a QUEUE of many small tasks (PRD with user
350: stories, issue list, maintenance backlog) to be executed across multiple
351: fresh-context iterations — supervised one-shot runs or bounded AFK batches.
352: A single feature/bugfix stays C2; an audit stays C4. If no durable backlog
353: file exists yet, create it FIRST (step 1) — the loop's source of truth is on
354: disk, never in chat.
355: 
356: **The pattern (state on disk, never in context):** each iteration starts
357: with a fresh context window, reorients from disk, completes exactly ONE
358: backlog item, proves it, commits, and exits. Progress lives in the ledger +
359: chronicle + git history, so a context reset loses nothing. (This is the
360: Ralph pattern; vibeweaver's inner loop — §A4.1, cap=5 / stall=3× — bounds
361: each single item, while the outer loop's bound is the iteration budget plus
362: the empty backlog.) Advisory: a task estimated beyond ~10 inner-loop
363: iterations SHOULD route here by default — shallow-fill contexts retrieve
364: best, and each fresh window dodges accumulated retrieval degradation
365: (arXiv:2609.36322 phase sensitivity); this is guidance, not a gate.
366: 
367: 1. **Backlog ledger (machine-checkable stop condition):**
368:    `tests/backlog.json` — one object per item:
369:    `{id, title, acceptanceCriteria: [], priority, passes: false, dependsOn: []}`.
370:    `passes` flips true ONLY with executed-test evidence (COV-1 applies per
371:    item). Items are sized to Lane S; anything bigger is split BEFORE
372:    entering the loop — an oversized item exhausts the context mid-item,
373:    which is the classic outer-loop failure. **Mechanism:**
374:    `python3 scripts/backlog_check.py` (copy from the skill) fails a
375:    `passes:true` item that no `tests/verification_log.md` /
376:    `tests/progress.txt` line names — run it per iteration and at loop end.
377: 2. **Progress chronicle (append-only):** `tests/progress.txt` — each
378:    iteration APPENDS: item id, what changed, check results, one note for
379:    the next iteration. NEVER rewrites history (append-only survives
380:    compaction; rewriting loses it). Curated lessons still go to memory/
381:    per A7.9 — progress.txt is the raw chronicle, memory/ the distilled one.
382: 3. **Iteration cycle:** reorient (§3.3: backlog.json → progress.txt tail →
383:    git log; an item that hits a FAIL opens a `tests/working_note.md` per
384:    §A7.15 — item-scoped, deleted when the item completes) → pick the
385:    highest-priority item with `passes:false` and all
386:    `dependsOn` satisfied — COMPUTE the frontier (a jq/gh query), never
387:    reconstruct it from prose → work ONLY that item under the full §1
388:    covenant (COV-9 baseline, §A4.1/§A4.7 loop, §A4.8 RED) → commit ONLY
389:    when green. A red commit poisons every later iteration's baseline;
390:    CI-green-per-commit is the loop's immune system.
391: 4. **Stop conditions (explicit, never vibes):** `COMPLETE` — every item
392:    `passes:true` · `BLOCKED` — needs a human → §3.4 PAUSED packet ·
393:    `DECIDE` — ambiguity → ADR (AUTO) / ask (GUIDED) · iteration budget
394:    exhausted — NOT a failure: read the chronicle, top up the budget, rerun.
395: 5. **HITL before AFK:** run the first iteration(s) supervised (one item,
396:    review the diff, refine the backlog). Only after the cycle proves green
397:    run bounded batches (e.g. 5–10 iterations). Never an unbounded
398:    while-true loop.
399: 6. **Feedback-loop ceiling:** the loop ships exactly what the repo's checks
400:    can prove. Weak typecheck/tests/Playwright → confident garbage at
401:    scale. Invest in checks BEFORE widening the batch size.
402: 7. **Steering mid-run:** corrections land where the next iteration actually
403:    reads them — a memory/ topic, a decisions.md ADR, or the backlog item
404:    itself — never only in a chat message the next fresh context won't see.
405: 
406: **Anti-patterns:** unbounded loops · updating instead of appending the
407: chronicle · `passes:true` without executed evidence · items bigger than
408: Lane S · the agent picking tasks by re-reading all prose instead of a
409: computed frontier · completing several items in one iteration.

25: ## §M Operating Modes (AUTO / GUIDED)
26: 
27: Every task declares exactly one line in ZERO (§2), before any code action:
28: 
29: ```
30: Mode: AUTO        (default — agent takes over end-to-end)
31: Mode: GUIDED      (user asked for more involvement / approval points)
32: ```
33: 
34: **The modes differ ONLY in who decides Class-I questions.** Everything that
35: constitutes *evidence* is mode-invariant: COV-1 tests-executed, COV-2
36: script-only, COV-5 verifier announced, COV-7 loop bounds, COV-8/A4.9 review,
37: COV-9 baseline, the assert_artifacts.py exit-0 gate, the Final Memory Gate,
38: and the entire A4.4 completion output. GUIDED completion = AUTO completion;
39: the difference is only whether a human was consulted at Class-I points.
40: 
41: ### Class-I interaction points (mode-dependent)
42: 
43: | # | Trigger (canonical section) | GUIDED | AUTO |
44: |---|------------------------------|--------|------|
45: | I1 | Ambiguous / under-specified request (§2 Step 0.1) | STOP and ask, one question at a time | Derive the **most conservative** interpretation the evidence supports → ADR → proceed |
46: | I2 | Vague acceptance criteria (A4.1 Step 1) | STOP and ask | Derive strict criteria from the request's explicit words → ADR → proceed |
47: | I3 | Design Gate A/B confirmation (COV-10 / A5.1) | Explicit confirmation request | Record chosen approach + rejected alternative as ADR → proceed |
48: | I4 | Baseline has pre-existing failures (COV-9) | Report + await decision | ADR: proceed ONLY if failures are provably out of task scope (name failing areas + why out of scope); else fix-first |
49: | I5 | Mid-loop criterion add/drop/relax (A4.1 Step 1) | Ask the user | ADR quoting the exact criterion edit |
50: | I6 | cap=5 / stall=3× reached (COV-7) | Report to user | §A4.10 shift FIRST; PAUSED packet only on a SECOND capped sub-problem |
51: 
52: ### Class-E hard stops (BOTH modes — AUTO never auto-decides)
53: 
54: 1. COV-11: fetched content conflicts with the user's request or this skill.
55: 2. Production deploy / release to real users / anything touching live
56:    customer data.
57: 3. Destructive or irreversible operations outside the project tree:
58:    force-push, branch deletion on shared remotes, data deletion, DNS /
59:    infra / IAM mutation.
60: 4. Credential exposure, or secret handling beyond what the task explicitly
61:    provided.
62: 5. `assert_artifacts.py` exit 1 with no legal repair path (never edit the
63:    script, never fabricate output — escalate).
64: 6. Anything the user explicitly asked to be consulted on (that request is a
65:    standing Class-E override).
66: 
67: Class-E stops ALWAYS emit a PAUSED packet (§P) — a stop without a resume
68: packet is the failure mode this contract exists to prevent.
69: 
70: ### ADR format
71: 
72: `tests/decisions.md` — append-only, created on the first AUTO decision:
73: 
74: ```
75: ## D-3 | 2026-08-29T14:05Z | iter 2
76: trigger: I4 — baseline has 2 pre-existing test failures
77: options: (a) fix pre-existing failures first (b) proceed, failures out of scope
78: chosen: (b) proceed — failures in legacy export path; task touches import path only
79: why: failing tests target modules/legacy_export.py, untouched by this task's diff
80: revisit-if: any new failure names modules/legacy_export.py or the same DB table
81: ```
82: 
83: Rules: one block per decision · `why:` must be falsifiable · `revisit-if:`
84: names an observable condition · never rewrite an old ADR (append a new one
85: superseding it). The completion output adds `[Decisions] N auto-decisions →
86: tests/decisions.md` before the 8-column table.
87: 
88: **Proactive ADRs** (no Class-I stop fired — e.g. a design-doc decision):
89: record one only when ALL three hold — hard to reverse · surprising without
90: context · the result of a real trade-off; skip otherwise (obvious or
91: reversible choices need no ADR).
92: 
93: **User veto path:** the user may veto any ADR post-hoc (it is in the repo
94: history). A veto is recorded as feedback memory (A7.9), the affected work is
95: redone in the next change-wave (own COV-9 baseline), and the veto reason
96: joins the project's ⛔/feedback entries.
97: 
98: **AUTO runaway bound:** AUTO buys autonomy, not license to spin. At most ONE
99: extra autonomous direction per stop type (I6: one §A4.10 shift before any
100: pause). ≥3 ADRs on the SAME sub-problem → the next stop is a PAUSED packet
101: regardless of mode.

105: ## §P PAUSED / Resume Contract
106: 
107: Every turn that stops for a gate — either mode, Class-I or Class-E — MUST
108: end with BOTH:
109: 
110: 1. `tests/paused_state.md` written with the packet below.
111: 2. The same one-liner as the LAST line of the reply (human-visible):
112: 
113: ```
114: [PAUSED] gate=<name> | question=<one line> | options=<2-3> | default-if-continue=<option> | state=<wave, files touched, next step>
115: ```
116: 
117: Field semantics: `gate:` names the rule that fired (I4 / COV-9 · I6 /
118: cap-stall · Class-E: COV-11 …) · `options:` are the 2-3 candidate actions ·
119: `default-if-continue:` is what the agent will do on an unqualified
120: "continue" · `state:` names the change-wave, the files already touched, and
121: the literal next step.
122: 
123: **Resume semantics:** a user "continue" (or any reply that does not pick an
124: option) = approval of `default-if-continue`. It is NOT a re-plan: the agent
125: does not re-derive context, re-ask settled questions, or restart the loop.
126: On resume: delete/clear `tests/paused_state.md`, append
127: `- resumed: <default> approved` to `tests/verification_log.md`, continue from
128: `state:`. A reply that picks a DIFFERENT option overrides the default; log
129: `- resumed: <chosen option> (user override)` instead.
130: 
131: **Re-entry order after a gap** (SKILL.md §3.3): paused_state.md (if present)
132: → tests/working_note.md (if present, §A7.15 — the live hypothesis ledger)
133: → tests/acceptance.md in full → verification_log.md tail (~40 lines; full
134: read only if <200 lines or inconsistent) → §1 covenant recall. Name the pass
135: (C1/C2/C4-C8) + first action in one line before acting.
136: 
137: **Batching:** ONE packet per pause, never a drip of questions. In GUIDED,
138: all pending Class-I questions of the current phase collapse into the single
139: packet's `options:`.
140: 
141: **Frontier rounds (GUIDED, ≥2 pending Class-I questions):** the single
142: packet is one *frontier round*:
143: 1. Number each question; each carries its own recommended answer (its
144:    `default-if-continue`).
145: 2. Order by dependency — a question whose answer depends on a still-open
146:    question belongs to the NEXT round, not this one.
147: 3. **Facts vs decisions:** never ask the user for a fact discoverable from
148:    the environment (files, git, config, tools) — look it up or dispatch a
149:    subagent. A running lookup is an unsettled prerequisite: questions
150:    downstream of it wait; ask the rest of the frontier now. Only *decisions*
151:    go to the user.
152: 4. Termination: frontier empty = nothing left silently assumed → proceed.
153: 
154: This refines the per-phase collapse above; single-ambiguity clarification
155: (I1 · REFERENCE.md §A5.1 Gate A) stays one-question-at-a-time. AUTO is
156: unchanged (ADRs, no frontier).

160: ## S1. Spike (Feasibility Probe)
161: 
162: **Trigger:** the request is a feasibility question ("can we…?", "is it
163: possible…?", "quick and dirty is fine") whose deliverable is an ANSWER, not
164: code you keep. Classified at §3.1; route here instead of C1/C2.
165: 
166: 1. Present the question + probe plan in 2-3 sentences (what you will try and
167:    how you will judge it). GUIDED: get a nod first. AUTO: write the probe's
168:    pass/fail question into `tests/acceptance.md` as the criteria.
169: 2. Investigate as cheaply as correctness allows. No design docs, no plan
170:    document, no §A4.8 TDD — the probe is throwaway by definition. §2 ZERO
171:    research still applies (a spike is not a license to guess).
172: 3. Report findings as a recommendation (feasible / not / under-what-
173:    conditions), probe evidence (logs, transcripts) under `tests/`.
174: 4. **Anything built stays labeled throwaway. Keeping spike code = a new
175:    request:** reclassify at §3.1 (usually C2) with its own COV-9 baseline —
176:    probe code never drifts into production ungated.
177: 5. Completion: the A4.4 table + gate line as usual; evidence is the probe
178:    log. `HARD-GATE-2=na` when nothing was built or started (state why).

182: ## C4. Audit (Read-Only Task)
183: 
184: **Trigger:** the primary deliverable is a review/report of an existing
185: codebase — code audit, security review, architecture assessment, migration
186: readiness check. NOT for fixing: fixes discovered by an audit become a
187: follow-up C2 task (record them in the report's remediation section).
188: 
189: **Read-only boundary:** no source, config, or script edits anywhere in the
190: target repo. Writes are limited to: `docs/AUDIT_<date>_<slug>.md`,
191: `tests/acceptance.md`, `tests/verification_log.md`, `tests/decisions.md`,
192: `memory/`. Violating the boundary voids the audit (the deliverable is
193: trust).
194: 
195: Binding order:
196: 
197: 1. `0 §2 ZERO + Mode line → 1 scope & criteria`: decompose the audit
198:    request into explicit, individually-checkable criteria — coverage areas
199:    (which modules/paths/qualities), depth, output language — into
200:    `tests/acceptance.md` (first line `> cap=5  stall=3×` preserved; COV-7
201:    bound applies to the audit pass itself). Ambiguity → Class-I rules.
202: 2. `2 READ-ONLY pass`: systematic inspection per criterion. Use search
203:    tools + reads; keep evidence quotes (file:line + 1-2 line excerpt) as you
204:    go — an audit note without a locator is not a finding candidate.
205: 3. `3 findings`: each finding = severity (Critical / Important / Minor) ·
206:    dimension (`Bugs` logic/edge cases · `Security` injection/authz/secrets/
207:    attacker-controlled input · `Compliance` matches stated requirements) ·
208:    file:line · why it matters · **PoC command or quoted-code argument**.
209:    A finding without repro/quote evidence is NOT a finding — it is a
210:    hypothesis; verify or drop it. Nit cap: itemize at most 5 Minors, count
211:    the rest.
212: 4. `4 independent verification`: Critical + Important findings are verified
213:    by a fresh-brain subagent (opencode `task`, READ-ONLY) given the finding
214:    list + PoCs — verdict per finding: CONFIRMED / REFUTED / UNCERTAIN.
215:    REFUTED → recorded as ruling, never silently dropped. UNCERTAIN →
216:    downgrade to "suspected" in the report.
217: 5. `5 report`: `docs/AUDIT_<date>_<slug>.md` — scope & method · findings
218:    (verified, with evidence) · remediation plan (ordered, each item = a
219:    future C2 task) · what was NOT covered (named, with reason).
220: 6. `6 completion`: A4.4 table + gate line with `Loop executed: no` ·
221:    `HARD-GATE-1: NO-TEST-NO-DONE=na` (zero code change — the *evidence* is
222:    the PoC outputs, which MUST be executed and logged to
223:    `verification_log.md` as `- audit-evidence:` lines) · `Code review: N/A`
224:    with `A4.9 not triggered` reason. COV-9 skipped (nothing modified).

228: ## C5. Deploy Workflow
229: 
230: **Trigger:** the task releases a build to an environment (staging, prod,
231: app store, server, container registry). Engineering standard stands
232: (ENGINEERING_STD §A8): **production deploys are human-confirmed — the agent
233: prepares (build, changelog, rollback path); the user authorizes the
234: production action.** C5 makes that rule mechanical.
235: 
236: Binding order:
237: 
238: 1. `0 §2 ZERO + Mode line → 1 pre-deploy checklist` (ALL must be green
239:    before the deploy action):
240:    - baseline GREEN on the release commit (COV-9, own change-wave);
241:    - pending DB migrations dry-run in a throwaway env (or documented N/A);
242:    - **rollback script exists**: `script/deploy/rollback.sh` (+ `.bat`) or
243:      documented manual rollback path — writing the rollback path IS part of

266: ## C6. Ops / Incident Workflow
267: 
268: **Trigger:** live breakage, alarms, user-reported production failure, or
269: routine maintenance waves (dependency upgrades, cert rotation, backup
270: restore checks).
271: 
272: **Incident path** (something is broken NOW):
273: 
274: 1. `0 triage FIRST — evidence before fixes (A4.6 Phase 1)`: capture the
275:    failure state (logs, metrics, error output) BEFORE touching anything;
276:    reproduce or bound the blast radius; identify the last-known-good version
277:    (git tag/commit + deploy record).
278: 2. `1 incident record`: open `docs/POSTMORTEM_<date>_<slug>.md`
279:    (APPENDIX C6 postmortem template) with trigger → timeline → impact. It is a chain
280:    artifact: cite the alert/log that started it.
281: 3. `2 hotfix via C2`: full C2 discipline with ONE relaxation — the COV-9
282:    baseline is the pre-incident commit (or last-known-good deploy), and the
283:    baseline run may be skipped if the system is DOWN (state
284:    `COV-9 skipped — active incident, system unavailable; baseline =
285:    <last-known-good>` in the log). Every other gate applies.
286: 4. `3 verify`: fix + suite green + the ORIGINAL failure evidence re-captured
287:    (the exact symptom that started the incident must be shown resolved).
288: 5. `4 postmortem`: complete the record — root cause, fix commit hash,
289:    **one permanent regression case** added to the test suite so the incident
290:    can never recur silently.
291: 6. `5 memory`: ⛔ (if ≥3 failures preceded the fix) / ❌ failed attempts /
292:    feedback per A7.9 + A4.4 completion table.
293: 
294: **Maintenance path** (nothing is broken): dependency upgrades and similar
295: waves run as C2 with a bound — **≤5 upgrades per change-wave**, each wave
296: gets its own COV-9 baseline + suite run; a red wave stops the batch (don't
297: mix 10 upgrades into one undiagnosable wave). One upgrade per commit inside
298: the wave, so bisect works.

302: ## C7. Non-Web Runtime (CLI / Library / Batch / Pipeline)
303: 
304: **Trigger:** the change's runtime surface is NOT a browser page (→ §A4.1)
305: and NOT an HTTP API (→ §A4.7): CLI output, library behavior, data pipeline,
306: batch job, daemon without HTTP.
307: 
308: **1. Profile:** write `tests/project_profile.json` in the FIRST change-wave:
309: `{"profile": "cli"}` (CLI/batch/pipeline) or `{"profile": "library"}`

312: to whatever lifecycle scripts the project actually has (a library's
313: `script/` may hold only test/release helpers — that's fine; the profile
314: documents why start/stop/restart don't exist).

316: **2. Acceptance criteria over OBSERVABLE output:** each criterion names a
317: checkable runtime observation — exit code for given input · stdout/stderr
318: content (exact or pattern) · files written (path + content shape) · timing
319: bound · golden-output equality. "Works correctly" is not a criterion.

321: **3. Evidence (replaces Playwright):** per flow, save to `tests/`:
322: - invocation transcript: command line + full stdout/stderr + exit code
323:   (`tests/<flow>.run.log`);
324: - output diff against a golden file where output is deterministic
325:   (`tests/<flow>.diff`);
326: - for pipelines: the artifact produced (file path + checksum) logged.

332: **4. §A4.8 test-first** for all logic-bearing code (a library's public API
333: IS logic-bearing): RED → GREEN per the standard cycle.

336: (`verification_log.md`, `diagnosis:` on every FAIL), cap=5 / stall=3×,
337: §A4.10 on stall. For libraries also run the DOWNSTREAM check: import/use
338: the library from a throwaway consumer script (`tests/consumer_smoke.py`) —
339: green unit tests do not prove the package installs or imports.

347: ## C8. Outer-Loop Workflow (Backlog / Long-Running Batch)
348: 
349: **Trigger:** the user hands over a QUEUE of many small tasks (PRD with user
350: stories, issue list, maintenance backlog) to be executed across multiple
351: fresh-context iterations — supervised one-shot runs or bounded AFK batches.
352: A single feature/bugfix stays C2; an audit stays C4. If no durable backlog
353: file exists yet, create it FIRST (step 1) — the loop's source of truth is on
354: disk, never in chat.
355: 
356: **The pattern (state on disk, never in context):** each iteration starts
357: with a fresh context window, reorients from disk, completes exactly ONE
358: backlog item, proves it, commits, and exits. Progress lives in the ledger +
359: chronicle + git history, so a context reset loses nothing. (This is the
360: Ralph pattern; vibeweaver's inner loop — §A4.1, cap=5 / stall=3× — bounds
361: each single item, while the outer loop's bound is the iteration budget plus
362: the empty backlog.) Advisory: a task estimated beyond ~10 inner-loop
363: iterations SHOULD route here by default — shallow-fill contexts retrieve
364: best, and each fresh window dodges accumulated retrieval degradation
365: (arXiv:2609.36322 phase sensitivity); this is guidance, not a gate.
366: 
367: 1. **Backlog ledger (machine-checkable stop condition):**
368:    `tests/backlog.json` — one object per item:
369:    `{id, title, acceptanceCriteria: [], priority, passes: false, dependsOn: []}`.
370:    `passes` flips true ONLY with executed-test evidence (COV-1 applies per
371:    item). Items are sized to Lane S; anything bigger is split BEFORE
372:    entering the loop — an oversized item exhausts the context mid-item,
373:    which is the classic outer-loop failure. **Mechanism:**
374:    `python3 scripts/backlog_check.py` (copy from the skill) fails a
375:    `passes:true` item that no `tests/verification_log.md` /
376:    `tests/progress.txt` line names — run it per iteration and at loop end.
377: 2. **Progress chronicle (append-only):** `tests/progress.txt` — each
378:    iteration APPENDS: item id, what changed, check results, one note for
379:    the next iteration. NEVER rewrites history (append-only survives
380:    compaction; rewriting loses it). Curated lessons still go to memory/
381:    per A7.9 — progress.txt is the raw chronicle, memory/ the distilled one.
382: 3. **Iteration cycle:** reorient (§3.3: backlog.json → progress.txt tail →
383:    git log; an item that hits a FAIL opens a `tests/working_note.md` per
384:    §A7.15 — item-scoped, deleted when the item completes) → pick the
385:    highest-priority item with `passes:false` and all
386:    `dependsOn` satisfied — COMPUTE the frontier (a jq/gh query), never
387:    reconstruct it from prose → work ONLY that item under the full §1
388:    covenant (COV-9 baseline, §A4.1/§A4.7 loop, §A4.8 RED) → commit ONLY
389:    when green. A red commit poisons every later iteration's baseline;
390:    CI-green-per-commit is the loop's immune system.
391: 4. **Stop conditions (explicit, never vibes):** `COMPLETE` — every item
392:    `passes:true` · `BLOCKED` — needs a human → §3.4 PAUSED packet ·
393:    `DECIDE` — ambiguity → ADR (AUTO) / ask (GUIDED) · iteration budget
394:    exhausted — NOT a failure: read the chronicle, top up the budget, rerun.
395: 5. **HITL before AFK:** run the first iteration(s) supervised (one item,
396:    review the diff, refine the backlog). Only after the cycle proves green
397:    run bounded batches (e.g. 5–10 iterations). Never an unbounded
398:    while-true loop.
399: 6. **Feedback-loop ceiling:** the loop ships exactly what the repo's checks
400:    can prove. Weak typecheck/tests/Playwright → confident garbage at
401:    scale. Invest in checks BEFORE widening the batch size.
402: 7. **Steering mid-run:** corrections land where the next iteration actually
403:    reads them — a memory/ topic, a decisions.md ADR, or the backlog item
404:    itself — never only in a chat message the next fresh context won't see.
405: 
406: **Anti-patterns:** unbounded loops · updating instead of appending the
407: chronicle · `passes:true` without executed evidence · items bigger than
408: Lane S · the agent picking tasks by re-reading all prose instead of a
409: computed frontier · completing several items in one iteration.

import unittest

from rle import rle_decode, rle_encode


class TestRleEncodeContract(unittest.TestCase):
    """Criterion #2: rle_encode returns a list of (count, byte) int tuples,
    count >= 1."""

    def test_returns_list_of_int_tuples(self):
        result = rle_encode(b"aabbc")
        self.assertIsInstance(result, list)
        for item in result:
            self.assertIsInstance(item, tuple,
                "encode must return (count, byte) tuples, got %r" % (item,))
            self.assertIsInstance(item[0], int,
                "count must be int, got %r" % (item[0],))
            self.assertIsInstance(item[1], int,
                "byte must be int, got %r" % (item[1],))
            self.assertGreaterEqual(item[0], 1,
                "count must be >= 1, got %r" % (item[0],))
            self.assertTrue(0 <= item[1] <= 255,
                "byte out of 0..255: %r" % (item[1],))

    def test_counts_and_bytes_in_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_encode(b"aaabbca"),
                         [(3, 97), (3, 98), (1, 99), (1, 97)])

    def test_single_byte_no_run(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_encode(b"q"), [(1, 113)])

    def test_empty_input(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_encode(b""), [])

    def test_all_byte_values(self):
        result = rle_encode(bytes(range(256)))
        self.assertEqual(result, [(1, b) for b in range(256)])


class TestRleRoundTrip(unittest.TestCase):
    """Criterion #3: decode(encode(x)) == x."""

    def test_roundtrip_empty(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode(rle_encode(b"")), b"")

    def test_roundtrip_single_byte(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode(rle_encode(b"\x00")), b"\x00")

    def test_roundtrip_multi_run(self):
        data = b"zzzzz ab bb "
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode(rle_encode(data)), data)

    def test_roundtrip_all_byte_values(self):
        data = bytes(range(256)) * 3
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode(rle_encode(data)), data)


class TestRleDecodeValidation(unittest.TestCase):
    """Criteria #4-#7: malformed pairs raise ValueError, never silent."""

    def test_zero_count_raises_value_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            rle_decode([(0, 65)])

    def test_negative_count_raises_value_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            rle_decode([(-3, 65)])

    def test_malformed_zero_count_returns_garbage(self):
        # The reported bug: count=0 / count<0 must NOT silently produce
        # truncated/empty output; it must be a ValueError.
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            rle_decode([(1, 66), (0, 65), (1, 67)])

    def test_non_int_count_raises_value_error(self):
        for bad in ("3", 2.5, None, True):  # True = bool, rejected (ADR D-1)
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                rle_decode([(bad, 65)])

    def test_non_int_byte_raises_value_error(self):
        for bad in ("a", 2.5, None, False):  # False = bool, rejected (ADR D-1)
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                rle_decode([(2, bad)])

    def test_out_of_range_byte_raises_value_error(self):
        for bad in (-1, 256):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                rle_decode([(1, bad)])


class TestRleDecodeValidBehavior(unittest.TestCase):
    """Criterion #8: valid pairs decode exactly as the as-is module did."""

    def test_valid_pairs_unchanged(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode([(2, 65), (1, 66), (5, 0)]),
                         b"AAB\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00")

    def test_empty_pairs(self):
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode([]), b"")

    def test_accepts_tuple_and_list_pairs_like_unpacking(self):
        # list-of-2 is accepted by 2-element unpacking; both are valid input
        # shapes for rle_decode per the task contract.
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode([[1, 65]]), b"A")
        self.assertEqual(rle_decode(frozenset()), b"")  # placeholder — see test below

- **The reported silent-garbage bug is closed at the source, not at the test.** Validation now happens before `out += bytes([b]) * count` (`rle.py:23-27`), so `[(1,66),(0,65),(1,67)]` can no longer truncate to `b'AB'`.

- **Encode tuple fix is structurally safe.** Immutability is enforced by construction recomposing the last tuple (`rle.py:9`) rather than in-place mutation that tuples would forbid (compared to the list-era `out[-1][0] += 1`). Decode side remains deliberately lenient about pair container type (`test_list_pairs_accepted`, `tests/test_rle.py:107`), so the only consumer-visible change is list→tuple, and tuple is what the contract mandates.
- **No scope creep in the commit.** Diff touches `rle.py` + 3 test-process docs only; all evidence artifacts (`*.run.log`, `.vibeweaver/`, `memory/`) are untracked. No other in-repo consumer of `rle_encode` exists (grep confirmed: round-trip callers only), so the tuple change ripples nowhere.
- **Wall-clock verification is consistent with the claims:** `python3 -m unittest tests.test_rle -v` → 18/18 OK; `python3 tests/consumer_smoke.py` → `PASS … 13 malformed cases all rejected with ValueError`, exit 0.

## Issues

**Minor — `Bugs`: non-2-sequence pairs raise `TypeError`, not `ValueError` (`rle.py:22-23`).** Probe: `rle_decode([65])` → `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable int object`; `rle_decode(5)` → `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable`. Wrong *sizes* are handled (3- and 1-tuples and strings-as-pairs all raise `ValueError`/`ValueError` via unpacking or the type check), but a structurally non-iterable pair is the one malformed shape that escapes the documented `ValueError` promise. Why it matters only modestly: the acceptance list (criteria #4–7) scopes `ValueError` to count/byte values, and nothing returns garbage — it raises — so it's a message/type consistency gap, not data loss. Suggested fix if desired: wrap unpacking in `try/except TypeError → raise ValueError` (one line), and note it in the docstring.

**Minor — `Bugs`: unbounded count allows `MemoryError` on oversized (but type-valid) counts (`rle.py:28`).** Probe: `rle_decode([(10**18, 65)])` → `MemoryError`. Why it matters: the contract sets no upper bound so this is out-of-spec, and the failure is fail-safe (raises, no garbage), but a library decode function that can attempt a 1 EB allocation from caller data is a soft denial-of-service surface with zero test coverage. Optional future bound (e.g. against `len` limits) is speculative per Simplicity-First, so flag only.

**Minor — `Compliance`: `rle_encode` performs no input-type check, so `rle_encode("aa")` → `[(2, 'a')]` — non-int "bytes" escape the `rle_encode` guarantee (`rle.py:4-12`).** Why it matters: the contract says `rle_encode` "must return a list of (count, byte) int pairs"; for `str` input that invariant silently breaks (bytes/bytearray/memoryview are all safe). Decode-side tests pin `0..255 int` bytes, but the encode side is only exercised with `bytes` fixtures, so the asymmetry between the two functions' type discipline is untested and undocumented. Correction of the encode docstring or a one-line `if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)): raise TypeError` would close it.

**Verified non-issues (probed, no action needed):** negative zero count `-0` → `ValueError` (it equals `0 < 1`); negative zero byte `-0` → accepted as `b'\x00'`, which is contract-correct since `-0 == 0 ∈ 0..255`; `2.5`/`3.0` floats → `ValueError` (int-valued floats correctly rejected, stricter-than-minimum); `True`/`False` in both slots → `ValueError`; valid-input regression `[(2,65),(1,66),(5,0)]` → exactly `b"AAB\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"` (criterion #8 preserved); caller unpacking patterns (`for c, b in pairs`, `tuple(pairs[0])`) all work.

3 minor findings, itemized above; no additional minor findings to summarize.

**ready**

14: ## A7.1 MEMORY.md — The Index
15: 
16: `memory/MEMORY.md` is the **entrypoint**. It is loaded into context at the
17: start of every session. It acts as a table of contents — not the memory content
18: itself.
19: 
20: **Format:**
21: ```markdown
22: # Project Memory Index
23: 
24: ## User Context
25: - [User Role & Preferences](user_role_prefs.md) — Senior backend engineer, prefers explicit error handling
26: - [Code Style Preferences](user_code_style.md) — Always use TypeScript strict mode, no any
27: 
28: ## Feedback — Validated Approaches
29: - [Keep Using Test DB](feedback_testing.md) — Use test containers, never mock DB in integration tests
30: - [Bundled PRs for Auth](feedback_auth_prs.md) — Single PR for tightly coupled auth refactors
31: 
32: ## Feedback — Corrections
33: - [Don't Use Raw SQL in Routes](feedback_no_raw_sql.md) — Always go through repository layer
34: 
35: ## Project Context
36: - [Q4 Deadlines](project_q4_deadlines.md) — Merge freeze 2026-03-05, release cutoff 2026-03-12
37: 
38: ## External References
39: - [Grafana Dashboard](reference_grafana.md) — Production metrics at grafana.example.com/d/abc123
40: 
41: ## Fix Tracking
42: - ⛔ [Forbidden: Direct DB Access from Routes](fix_forbidden_db_routes.md) — Never query DB from route handlers
43: - ✅ [Fix: Login Timeout](fix_login_timeout.md) — Session TTL mismatch between auth service and gateway
44: - ⏳ [Fix: Search Pagination](fix_search_pagination.md) — Pending user confirmation
45: 
46: ## Key Dependencies & Conventions
47: - `auth/` module must be loaded before `routes/` (circular dependency resolved via lazy import)
48: - WebSocket connections require explicit heartbeat every 30s
49: ```
50: 
51: **Caps:**
52: - **Loading cap:** **200 lines** or **25,000 bytes** (25KB) — whichever comes first. If the index is larger, **truncate on load** and append a warning:
53:   ```
54:   > WARNING: MEMORY.md is over the limit. Only part was loaded. Consolidate entries or move detail into topic files.
55:   ```
56: - **Consolidation trigger:** When the index grows beyond **150 lines** or **20KB**, run consolidation at the end of the session (see A7.13).
57: - Keep each index line to one line under ~150 characters
58:

61: ## A7.2 Topic Files — One Per Memory Entry
62: 
63: Each memory entry is a **separate `.md` file** with YAML frontmatter. This enables on-demand loading — only the most relevant topic files are loaded per session.
64: 
65: **Frontmatter format:**
66: ```yaml
67: ---
68: name: Short descriptive title
69: description: One-line description used to decide relevance in future sessions — be specific
70: type: user | feedback | project | reference | fix
71: date: 2026-06-28
72: status: ⛔ | ✅ | ⏳   # Required for fix type only
73: commit: abc1234      # Required for fix type only — short hash of the change this memory describes
74: file_refs:          # Optional — for fix entries that cite specific files; enables stale-ref auto-detection (A7.6 rule 8)
75:   - path: backend/app/auth/config.py
76:     range: "40-50"         # approx line range cited
77:     sha_at_time: 8f3a2c1   # git blob sha at fix time: git rev-parse <commit>:<path>
78: last_validated: 2026-06-28 # Optional — last session that re-verified this entry
79: ---
80: ```
81: 
82: **Body structure (feedback/project types):**
83: - Lead with the **rule or fact** itself
84: - **Why:** — the reason (past incident, constraint, strong preference)
85: - **How to apply:** — when/where this guidance kicks in, edge cases
86: 
87: **Example — feedback type:**
88: ```markdown
89: ---
90: name: Don't Mock DB in Integration Tests
91: description: Never use in-memory SQLite or mocked repositories in tests that touch the database
92: type: feedback
93: date: 2026-06-28
94: ---
95: 
96: # Don't Mock the Database in Integration Tests
97: 
98: **Why:** Prior incident where mock/prod divergence masked a broken migration. The mock SQLite accepted NULL in a NOT NULL column that PostgreSQL rejected.
99: 
100: **How to apply:** When writing tests for DB-touching code, use test containers or a real test database. Mocking is acceptable only for pure unit tests that don't exercise SQL.
101: ```
102: 
103: **Example — project type:**
104: ```markdown
105: ---
106: name: Q4 Merge Freeze
107: description: Team release schedule with merge freeze and cutoff dates for Q4 2026
108: type: project
109: date: 2026-03-01
110: ---
111: 
112: # Q4 Merge Freeze
113: 
114: Merge freeze begins **2026-03-05**. Mobile team is cutting a release branch.
115: 
116: **How to apply:** Flag any non-critical PR work scheduled after that date. Critical bugfixes still allowed with release-manager approval.
117: ```
118: 
119: **Example — fix type (unverified):**
120: ```markdown
121: ---
122: name: Fix Login Timeout
123: description: Session TTL mismatch causing premature logout on the login page
124: type: fix
125: date: 2026-06-28
126: status: ⏳
127: commit: a1b2c3d
128: ---
129: 
130: # Fix Login Timeout
131: 
132: **Problem:** Users reported being logged out after ~5 minutes of inactivity on the login page.
133: 
134: **Root Cause:** Session TTL was set to 300s in auth service but 3600s in API gateway. The gateway's longer TTL masked the issue until the auth service expired the session first.
135: 
136: **Correct Fix:** Aligned both TTLs to 1800s in `backend/app/auth/config.py:42` and `gateway/nginx.conf:15`.
137: 
138: **Failed Approaches (DO NOT retry):**
139: - Increasing only the auth service TTL without checking gateway — still caused mismatch
140: - Adding a client-side refresh timer — papered over the issue, didn't fix root cause
141: 
142: **Files:** `backend/app/auth/config.py`, `gateway/nginx.conf`
143: **Status:** ⏳ Pending — awaiting user confirmation
144: ```

150: ## A7.3 Memory Types
151: 
152: Memories are constrained to types capturing context NOT derivable from the current project state:
153: 
154: | Type | What to Save | When to Save |
155: |------|-------------|--------------|
156: | **user** | User's role, goals, skill level, preferences | When you learn any detail about the user's perspective or expertise |
157: | **feedback** | Corrections AND confirmations on approach | When user says "don't do X", OR confirms "yes exactly, keep doing that" |
158: | **project** | Ongoing work, goals, deadlines, team context | When you learn who is doing what, why, or by when. Convert relative dates to absolute |
159: | **reference** | Pointers to external resources (issue tracker, dashboards, docs) | When you learn where to find up-to-date information outside the project |
160: | **fix** | Bug fixes and modifications — root cause, correct fix, failed attempts | After every code change (see State Flow Rules below) |
161: 
162: **Critical: Record from both failure AND success.** If you only save corrections, you will drift away from approaches the user has already validated.
163:

166: ## A7.4 What NOT to Save
167: 
168: - Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — derivable by reading the project
169: - Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative
170: - Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context
171: - Anything already documented in README or other project docs
172: - Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context
173:

176: ## A7.5 Trust Tiers (for fix entries)
177: 
178: | Tier | Trust Level | Purpose |
179: |------|-------------|---------|
180: | ⛔ **Forbidden** | Highest — hard constraints | Methods proven to fail. Agent MUST NOT retry. |
181: | ✅ **Verified** | High — confirmed by user | Root cause, correct fix, failed approaches. Primary reference. |
182: | ⏳ **Unverified** | Low — may be wrong | Agent's modifications awaiting user validation. Informational only. |
183: | ❌ **Failed**    | Negation of ⏳       | An ⏳ that failed a later check or got reimplemented badly. Same hard constraints as permissibility. |
184: 
185: **Core principle: unverified modifications are NOT facts. Never treat ⏳ entries as proven solutions.**

189: ## A7.6 On Every Skill Invocation — Memory Loading
190: 
191: When the skill triggers, load project memory in this order:
192: 
193: 1. **Check if `memory/MEMORY.md` exists**
194:    - YES → Read it (first 200 lines / 25KB automatically loaded via truncation)
195:    - NO → Check if old `MODIFY.html` exists. If yes, **migrate it** to the `memory/` directory structure (see A7.11). If neither exists, this is a fresh project — create `memory/MEMORY.md` with template from [MEMORY_TEMPLATES.md](MEMORY_TEMPLATES.md).
196: 
197: 2. **Scan the index** — For each section (User Context, Feedback, Project Context, External References, Fix Tracking), note the entries relevant to the current task.
198: 
199: 3. **Search before selecting** — Extract keywords from the user's request (problem symptom, feature name, file/module names, error messages). Use the `grep` tool to search `memory/*.md` for topic files whose names, descriptions, or bodies mention those keywords. This catches relevant memories whose index descriptions may not be obvious.
200: 
201: 4. **Select top 3-5 most relevant topic files** — Combine index scan + search results. Prioritize in this order:
202:    - ⛔ **Forbidden** entries touching the same area
203:    - ❌ **Failed** attempts with the same symptom
204:    - ✅ **Verified** fixes for the same files or problem
205:    - ⏳ **Unverified** attempts for the same problem
206:    - **Feedback** entries about the relevant approach or file
207:    Load only those files.
208: 
209: 5. **Verify references before trusting** — For any loaded memory that names specific files, functions, classes, configs, or line numbers, read the current code to confirm they still exist and mean the same thing. If a reference is stale, update or remove the memory entry and note the staleness.
210: 
211: 6. **Check for staleness** — For any loaded topic file with a `date` older than 14 days from today, display:
212:    ```
213:    > ⚠️ This memory is N days old. Memories are point-in-time observations — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before acting.
214:    ```
215: 
216: 7. **Check ⏳ Unverified entries** — If the user's current request overlaps an ⏳ fix entry in problem, symptom, affected file, or attempted solution, treat it as a failure signal. Mark that entry ❌ before attempting a new direction (see A7.7 Implicit Failure Detection).
217: 
218: 8. **✅ Verified staleness rule** — a ✅ entry is NOT immune to staleness; it only means it was verified at the commit recorded. When loading a ✅ fix entry:
219:    - If its `last_validated` is absent or >14 days old → mark it ⏳ again with a `stale: needs re-verification` note and re-verify before trusting.
220:    - If it has `file_refs[*].sha_at_time` and that ≠ current `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (or the ref is absent and the file moved) → same treatment: demote to ⏳ with a stale-refs note; re-verify code references against current code before acting on it.
221:    - A stale ✅ provides context but MUST NOT be relied on for downstream decisions until re-verified this session.
222:

225: ## A7.7 State Flow Rules (for fix-tracking entries)
226: 
227: ```
228: Agent modifies code
229:   ↓
230: Agent runs Playwright / automated tests
231:   ├─ Tests FAIL → create fix topic file with status ❌, try different direction
232:   └─ Tests PASS → create fix topic file with status ⏳ (NOT as ✅)
233:         ↓
234:   Next session begins:
235:     ├─ User gives same/similar prompt → auto-mark ⏳ as ❌, try different direction
236:     ├─ User explicitly says "still broken" → mark ⏳ as ❌, try different direction
237:     └─ User confirms "works" / no further complaint → promote to ✅ Verified
238: ```
239: 
240: **Implicit Failure Detection: if the user's current request overlaps an ⏳ fix entry in problem, symptom, affected file, or attempted solution, treat it as a failure signal. Mark that entry ❌ before attempting a new direction.**
241: 
242: **≥3 failures on same problem → escalate all failed methods to a ⛔ Forbidden topic file.**

246: ## A7.8 Pre-Change Guardrails
247: 
248: Before implementing any change:
249: 1. Check ⛔ **Forbidden** entries — do NOT use any listed method
250: 2. Scan ✅ **Verified** fix entries for files you are about to touch — learn from confirmed solutions
251: 3. Scan ⏳ **Unverified** fix entries for the current problem — if a pending entry exists, acknowledge it and explain why this attempt takes a different direction
252: 4. Check **Feedback** entries for relevant guidance on approach
253: 5. When touching a ⛔ flagged area, explicitly state why your approach avoids the forbidden pattern

257: ## A7.9 Post-Session Memory Writing ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
258: 
259: **At the end of every session, before outputting the completion table, you MUST review and write memories:**
260: 
261: 1. **Review the conversation** — Identify new information worth persisting across sessions
262: 2. **Write topic files** for each new entry in `memory/` with proper frontmatter
263: 3. **Update MEMORY.md index** — Add pointer lines for new entries. Remove pointers to stale/removed entries
264: 4. **Fix-tracking rules:**
265:    - Write fix entries as `status: ⏳` if tests passed, `status: ❌` if tests failed
266:    - **Never write `status: ✅`** — only user confirmation can verify a fix
267:    - Include the commit short hash in the frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`) for every fix entry
268:    - Include **Failed Approaches** and **Rejected Alternatives** in fix topic bodies so future sessions do not rediscover the same dead ends
269:    - If ≥3 failures preceded this fix, create/update a ⛔ Forbidden entry
270: 5. **Record feedback memories** when user corrects or confirms approach during the session
271: 6. **Record project memories** when you learn about goals, deadlines, or team context
272: 7. **Check MEMORY.md caps** — If index exceeds 150 lines or 20KB, consolidate before adding more
273: 8. **Resolve the task working note** — distill `tests/working_note.md` (§A7.15) into the permanent topic files, then delete it (machine-checked by group 19 on the `--final` run)
274: 
275: **The checklist item "Memory topic file written to memory/" is MANDATORY for
276: any task that produced a lesson — lesson-triggered, not per-task ritual.**
277: Lesson-less tasks (Class DOC / trivial changes, §V11.3) state
278: `- memory: na (<why no lesson>)` in `tests/verification_log.md` instead of
279: writing filler topics (A7.1 "what NOT to save" — a forced empty topic is
280: worse than none).

284: ## A7.10 Final Memory Gate ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
285: 
286: Before outputting the completion table, you MUST pass this gate. If any check fails, return to A7.9 and fix it before declaring the task complete.
287: 
288: 1. **Memory files exist** — At least one new or updated topic file exists in `memory/` for this session (unless the task was purely informational and produced nothing persistable).
289: 2. **Index updated** — `memory/MEMORY.md` contains a pointer to the new topic file(s), and the index is under 200 lines / 25KB.
290: 3. **Fix entries have commit** — Every `type: fix` topic file written this session includes `commit: <short-hash>` in its frontmatter. **History-rewrite waves (Class-E `git filter-repo`, ENGINEERING_STD §A10.1) must complete the commit-map hash remap BEFORE passing this gate** — every `commit:` cited in `memory/**` and `tests/verification_log.md` is rewritten from `.git/filter-repo/commit-map` (copy, never retype a hash), then this gate re-checks them.
291: 4. **No stale references introduced** — Any file/function/line cited in new memories was verified against current code during this session.
292: 5. **Scratchpad cleaned (legacy)** — the pre-§A7.15 `memory/.session-scratchpad.md` is superseded by tests/working_note.md; if a legacy scratchpad exists, delete it after permanent memories are written.
293: 6. **Working note resolved** — If `tests/working_note.md` was created (§A7.15), its persistable content was distilled into the topic files written this session and the file itself is deleted. The completion-time `assert_artifacts.py --final` run (group 19) machine-checks the deletion.
294: 
295: **Failure response:**
296: - If a memory should have been written but was not, write it now and re-run this gate.
297: - If you genuinely have nothing persistable (rare), explicitly state "No memory written — task was informational only" in the completion table's `What Changed` column.
298: 
299: **Explicit reporting:** In the line immediately before the completion table, output a single summary line:
300: ```
301: [Memory Gate] Passed: N new/updated topic file(s) | Index updated: yes/no | Commit hashes present: yes/no/N/A | Scratchpad cleaned: yes/no/N/A
302: ```
303: or, when nothing persistable was produced (§V11.3 lesson-triggered):
304: ```
305: [Memory Gate] na (<why no lesson>) — gate line field: memory_gate: na
306: ```
307: Do not output the completion table until this line is present and all answers are truthful.

311: ## A7.11 Promoting to Verified & Migration from Old Format
312: 
313: **Promoting a fix to ✅ Verified:**
314: When user confirms a fix works (or next session has no complaint about it):
315: 1. Change `status: ⏳` → `status: ✅` in the topic file's frontmatter
316: 2. Fill in **Root Cause**, **Failed Approaches**, and **Rejected Alternatives** in the body
317: 3. Add the verified commit short hash to the frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`)
318: 4. Add `file_refs` (path + range + `sha_at_time` from `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`) for every file cited, and set `last_validated: <today>` — this makes the ✅ entry self-aging (A7.6 rule 8)
319: 5. Update the index line to show ✅ instead of ⏳
320: 6. If ≥3 failures preceded the fix, also create a ⛔ Forbidden entry
321: 
322: **Migrating from old MODIFY.html / MODIFY_COMPACT.html:**
323: If an old project has `MODIFY.html` or `MODIFY_COMPACT.html` but no `memory/` directory:
324: 1. Read the old file(s) completely
325: 2. Split each logical entry into a separate `memory/*.md` topic file with proper frontmatter
326: 3. Create `memory/MEMORY.md` with pointer lines for all entries
327: 4. Do NOT delete the old HTML files — they serve as archive
328: 5. This is a one-time migration; subsequent sessions use `memory/`
